newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Nearly 30,000 died on Russia's roads in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 30,000 died on Russia's roads in 1996.

text.p: Almost 30,000 people died in car accidents on Russia's roads in 1996, the State Automobile Inspectorate said on Thursday.
Nationwide police recorded 160,523 car accidents resulting in 29,468 deaths, Interfax news agency quoted the head of the inspectorate Vladimir Fyodorov as saying.
He did not give figures for the preceding year but Russian media said the total number of road deaths had fallen from 1995.
Experts say the number of road deaths in Russia is relatively high of badly maintained roads, poor driving and heavy drinking.
Russian cars are also lacking in modern safety features such as air bags and many drivers and passengers fail to wear seat belts.
Traffic police reported almost 50 million traffic violations by Russian drivers last year -- an increase of nearly five percent from 1995, Fyodorov said. Russia has a population of 150 million.
